recognize_zh: GMS 銀染下，綠色背景中可見大量黑色、極細且分支的絲狀菌，交織成團並呈放射狀向外延伸；菌絲寬度遠小於真菌菌絲，這種細絲狀分支細菌聚落符合放線菌（Actinomyces）菌落。
features: Dense black GMS-positive masses of very thin (under 1 um), branching filaments
Filaments radiate outward at the colony periphery and form tangled clumps
Filament width is far narrower than fungal hyphae, with no septate broad hyphae, yeast forms, or spores
Scattered short fragmented filaments in the adjacent light green counterstained debris
Background of green-stained inflammatory debris and fibrin
describe_en: GMS-stained section of the peritoneal nodule shows dense black-staining colonies composed of innumerable very thin, branching filaments that radiate outward at the periphery and form tangled clumps. The filaments are markedly narrower than fungal hyphae, and no broad septate hyphae, yeasts, or spores are identified. The surrounding light green counterstain highlights inflammatory debris with scattered short filament fragments. In conjunction with the sulfur granule on H&E and Gram positivity, findings are consistent with Actinomyces colonies of actinomycosis; the filing of this image under fungi reflects the silver stain rather than a fungal organism.

ddx.vs: Nocardia filaments are also GMS-positive and branching but are beaded, rarely form compact granules, and are positive on modified acid-fast stain.
Aspergillus hyphae are 3-6 um wide with regular septation and acute-angle branching, much broader than these thin bacterial filaments.
Fungal grains are composed of broad septate hyphae with swollen chlamydospores rather than delicate filaments under 1 um.

ddx.dx: Reticulin or elastic fibers highlighted by silver
ddx.vs: Connective tissue fibers are continuous, non-radiating strands within stroma rather than discrete colonies of short branching filaments.
